No UI code changed. All thirteen gates ran on this clean committed SHA; `git status --porcelain` was empty before them and HEAD was unchanged after, and `npm run build` reproduced the tracked dist/ byte-for-byte. The packaged artifact holds 312 files, one more than v0.5.1: docs/ is inside the package.json files list, so the merge-gate-pre-0.5.1.json archive written by the previous receipt commit is itself shipped. Receipt commits therefore change packaged files by construction, which is why each release re-runs the gates on a fresh baseline. Only receipt files change afterwards. No push, tag, release or installed-plugin update is performed by this receipt.

observedFailure.source: Field reports #11, #12 and #14 against the user's own data root on 2026-09-09, not an observation of these gates.
sequence: 14:03:52Z — a SessionStart maintenance wake handed the extractor model budget fe4a61c1, whose deadline_at had already passed. claimExtractionTarget claimed both pending targets first, incrementing attempts to 1, and the budget was only resolved later inside the model call.

reserveModelAttempt raised deadline exhaustion before inserting any model_work_attempts row, so no provider call was ever made, yet deferMemoryJobForModelBudget parked both jobs with available_at = now + 60min, observed in the database as available_at 15:03:52Z.
14:04:18Z — the same wake minted a fresh budget 26 seconds later, but every job it could have run was already in backoff, so its window expired unused.

14:23Z — a foreground `memex backfill extract` could not claim either job and reported HANDOFF (다른 러너가 처리 중), although lease_owner was NULL and no worker process existed. The operator was shown a phantom runner instead of a retry backoff.

15:11Z (#14, after v0.5.1 shipped) — budget 15af9e61 sat in state `active` with a deadline 52 minutes in the past. v0.5.1's pre-claim check reported the exhaustion but no longer wrote it, because the durable transition had only ever been a side effect of reserveModelAttempt on its way to throwing. Every foreground backfill deferred, `memex model-work resume --new-run` answered that the budget was still active, and an automatic wake was the operator's only remaining exit.

fix.#14: The exhaustion predicate and the durable transition are now one shared pair, resolveBudgetExhaustion and markModelBudgetExhausted, used by the pre-claim check, the attempt reservation, explicit exhaustion, the automatic wake and resume alike, so no path can report an exhaustion it does not record. The check stays read-only when the budget is genuinely fine: not even updated_at moves. `model-work resume --new-run` additionally settles a clock-dead active budget itself rather than refusing the operator's only exit, while a budget with real time left is still refused, and both workers now print the exact recovery command, `memex model-work resume <budget-id> --new-run`, with the real id.
fix.#12: findExhaustedModelBudgetForClaim resolves the job's durable budget before the claim and applies the same exhaustion predicate reserveModelAttempt uses, so a dead budget never costs an attempt; the pre-flight creates nothing, so an unbound job keeps its lazy-creation path. Because the pre-flight and the reservation are still separated by wall clock, deferMemoryJobForModelBudget takes an opt-in claimedAt: a deadline or window stop that follows a claim which reserved no provider attempt refunds that attempt and returns the job to pending at now. An attempts exhaustion keeps the old one-hour fence, because that budget really was spent.
fix.#11: claimMemoryJobById now reports which of its four refusal reasons applied — lease_held, backoff with the instant it becomes due, attempts_exhausted, cas — from the row the predicate already reads, with no extra query, no extra write and no change to what is claimable. CLAIM_REJECTION_REPORT is the single source for label, note, bucket and escalation, so the worker cannot print a label that disagrees with its own counters. The worker prints HANDOFF (lease held by another runner), DEFERRED (retry backoff until <ISO>) or SKIPPED (attempt cap reached), counts them as handoff / backoff-deferred / attempt-cap, and escalates only the attempt cap. `memex status` gains a matching backoff breakdown of pending plus the earliest retry time.

backfillScheduling.exitCodeContract: Unchanged. Backoff work stays inside the extract stage's pending count, so `memex backfill extract` still exits 2 for "completed with deferred work"; 0 and 1 keep their meanings and terminal `deferred` keeps its own.
backfillScheduling.regressions: test/model-budget-expired-state.test.ts (8 cases: the backfill claim defers without burning an attempt and settles the budget, a healthy budget is left untouched, resume --new-run is accepted on an untouched active budget whose deadline passed and still refused when real time remains, the whole issue walked back out as defer -> resume --new-run -> claim, and three automatic-wake variants covering a fresh budget minted and rebound in the same wake, the 1h cooldown settling the budget without minting, and the 24h rolling cap); test/backfill-cli-slice.test.mjs (a case pinning that the DEFERRED (budget_exhausted) line prints the exact resume command with the real budget id, asserting the durable state so the fixture reproduces the issue rather than its fix). Carried forward from v0.5.1: test/model-budget-stale-claim.test.ts (3 cases: a stale budget refuses the claim instead of spending an attempt and an hour of backoff, the fresh budget from the same wake claims the work immediately, and an unspent claim is refunded on a deadline stop while the attempts fence holds); test/claim-rejection-reason.test.ts (5 cases: backoff reported with its due time rather than a phantom runner, a live lease still reported as a handoff, an exhausted attempt cap reported as its own reason, the reason surfaced through runFactExtraction for the worker, and status counting backoff sessions with the earliest retry); test/backfill-cli-slice.test.mjs (1 added case reproducing the exact observed state — lease_owner NULL, no runner, future available_at — and pinning exit 2 with a deferred, not handoff, message). test/backfill-worker-execution.test.ts (10 cases) and test/worker-dist-contract.test.ts (9 cases) cover worker execution and the dist contract, including a dist predating claimReason falling back to the previous HANDOFF behaviour.
backfillScheduling.regressionFrom051Note: v0.5.1's pre-claim short-circuit removed the durable active -> exhausted transition that reserveModelAttempt used to perform on its way to throwing, which is what left budget 15af9e61 active-but-expired and unresumable.

testDeterminism.change: The v0.5.1 backfill claim fixtures pinned an absolute instant, `const T0 = new Date("2026-09-09T14:03:52.000Z")`, to mirror the reported incident. v0.5.2 rebases them on `const T0 = new Date()` in test/model-budget-stale-claim.test.ts, test/claim-rejection-reason.test.ts and the new test/model-budget-expired-state.test.ts, so the deadline and backoff arithmetic is relative to the run.
testDeterminism.whyItMattered: Those fixtures began failing the day after they were written. The v0.5.1 gates were run on 2026-09-09, the same date the fixtures pinned, so that receipt's green `npm test` was partly a property of the calendar. This is recorded rather than left implicit: the v0.5.1 receipt is accurate about what was observed, but its tests gate would not have reproduced on a later date without this change.
testDeterminism.verifiedHere: Confirmed by reading both files at the v0.5.1 merge commit and at this SHA; the current fixtures reference 2026-09-09 only in the comments that cite the incident.

releaseConclusion: All thirteen gates PASS on the clean v0.5.2 candidate 874f9554, each on its first attempt: typecheck, a build that reproduced the tracked dist/, 101 files / 1034 Vitest tests, 26 Codex slices, 107 total slices, installer, marketplace, packaged runtime (memex-0.5.2.tgz, 312 files, 9 MCP tools), offline lifecycle 9/9, the real-Chrome Memex Workspace E2E (10 check groups, 0 runtime errors), 82 Workspace unit tests and the benchmark contract. Isolated plugin validation passes all 11 substitute checks with matching 0.5.2 plugin and MCP server versions, and is PASS-WITH-NOTES only because the formal `codex plugin validate` subcommand does not exist in codex-cli 0.153.4. This release is a hotfix for a regression the previous release caused: v0.5.1's pre-claim budget check reported an exhaustion it no longer durably wrote, stranding budget 15af9e61 as active-but-expired with resume refusing it, and the exhaustion predicate and transition are now a single shared pair used by every path. Eight new isolated cases cover the defer, the resume, the full walk-back and three automatic-wake variants, and a CLI slice pins the printed recovery command against the issue's durable state. The v0.5.1 fixtures that pinned 2026-09-09 are now relative to the run clock; the v0.5.1 gates were themselves executed on that date, so that receipt's tests gate was partly calendar-dependent, which is recorded here rather than left implicit. The one added packaged file is this process's own v0.5.1 receipt archive, not product code. The full acceptance benchmark was NOT re-run and is carried forward as prior evidence measured on 236d7362. The v0.5.1 receipt is archived byte-for-byte as merge-gate-pre-0.5.2.json. Replaying the failing wake against the user's real data root, draining the live backlog, live user data, an authenticated Codex tier run, the formal plugin validator, benchmark numbers for this exact SHA, real-world performance and model quality are NOT_PROVEN.
